intended_object: For a finite Galois extension L/k and a k-algebra R, the k-subalgebra of R descended from an L-subalgebra P ⊆ L ⊗_k R: the set {r ∈ R | 1 ⊗ r ∈ P}. When P is Galois-stable, this is the subalgebra with L ⊗_k (descended P) = P. The meaning comes from the docstring ("honest preimage") and from its use in `baseChange_descended_eq` and `descended_isFiniteEtale`.
explanation:
The body first restricts the scalars of P from L to k, so P becomes a k-subalgebra of L ⊗[k] R. It then takes the preimage (`Subalgebra.comap`) under the k-algebra map `includeRight : R → L ⊗[k] R`, which sends r to 1 ⊗ r. The result is exactly {r ∈ R | 1 ⊗ r ∈ P}, as `mem_descended` states. This is the standard descent of a subalgebra. For a Galois-stable P the library proves `(descended P).baseChange L = P`, which is the expected Galois-descent statement.

Because of the section variables, the definition carries the `FiniteDimensional` and `IsGalois` hypotheses. The preimage itself only needs an algebra L over k. However, this is a thin named wrapper around Mathlib's general `Subalgebra.comap`, and it is meant for the Galois-descent setting, where its key property (`baseChange_descended_eq`) needs those hypotheses. So it is not a re-implementation of a more general construction at reduced generality. It needs no junk values and has no degenerate-case problems.

Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this descended subalgebra, so `mathlib_counterpart` is left empty. The general preimage operation it is built from is `Subalgebra.comap`.
